descriptors.concept_name: Key Managerial Personnel and Manager Definitions
descriptors.definition: Key Managerial Personnel include core officers like the Chief Executive Officer, Managing Director, Company Secretary, Whole-time Director, and Chief Financial Officer. A manager is an individual appointed under Board direction to manage the whole or substantially the whole of the company affairs.
inclusion: Officers designated under specific statutory clauses
Individuals heading the overall management of company affairs
exclusion: Departmental heads managing only specific sections of a company
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes a company-wide manager from sectional departmental heads

descriptors.concept_name: Appointment of Managing Director, Whole Time Director or Manager [Section 196]
descriptors.definition: Companies can appoint a managing director, whole-time director, or manager for a maximum term of five years at a time. Re-appointments cannot occur earlier than one year before the current term expires, and appointees must meet specific age and directorial qualification criteria.
inclusion: Appointments of managing directors, whole-time directors, and managers
Special resolution requirements for appointees over seventy years old
exclusion: Simultaneous appointment of both a managing director and a manager
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts general board appointments with statutory tenure limits and age restrictions

descriptors.definition: Specified classes of companies must employ mandatory whole-time key managerial personnel, including listed companies and public or private firms meeting paid-up capital thresholds. Furthermore, an individual cannot hold the dual positions of Chairperson and Managing Director or Chief Executive Officer simultaneously unless exempted by articles or multiple business structures.
instrument_references: Rule 8 and Rule 8A of Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014
inclusion: Listed companies and public companies with high share capital
Private companies meeting statutory capital thresholds requiring a company secretary
exclusion: Firms exempted due to engaging in multiple distinct businesses with separate chief executives
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates general executive hiring from mandatory KMP staffing rules

descriptors.definition: A company secretary is statutorily responsible for reporting compliance with applicable laws, ensuring adherence to secretarial standards, and facilitating board and general meetings. They also provide administrative guidance to directors and maintain official corporate governance records.
instrument_references: Rule 10 of Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014
inclusion: Advising directors on powers and duties
Representing the company before regulatory authorities
exclusion: Alteration of independent duties assigned to other statutory functionaries
nearby_distinctions: Separates routine administrative duties from statutory secretarial compliance functions

descriptors.concept_name: Company to Fix Limit With Regard to Remuneration [Section 200]
descriptors.definition: Companies lacking profits or having inadequate earnings may establish administrative limits for managerial remuneration within statutory bounds. When fixing such pay, the company must consider its financial position, operating performance, and proportionality relative to other executives.
instrument_references: Rule 6 of Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014
inclusion: Remuneration adjustments during periods of low or zero profit
Evaluation of professional qualifications and past performance
exclusion: Mandatory central government approval for inadequate profit remuneration after the specified effective date
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates profit-based payout limits from loss-period administrative ceilings

descriptors.concept_name: Overall Maximum Managerial Remuneration And Managerial Remuneration In Case Of Absence Or Inadequacy Of Profits [Section 197]
descriptors.definition: Public companies are restricted from paying total managerial remuneration exceeding eleven percent of net profits, with specific sub-limits applied to individual directors. These net profits are computed under statutory accounting guidelines specified for managerial compensation.
instrument_references: Schedule V of the Companies Act, 2013
inclusion: Limits applicable to public companies having profits
Thresholds expandable via special resolutions in general meetings
exclusion: Private companies which are exempt from these specific statutory caps
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts aggregate company-wide managerial caps with individual director limits

descriptors.concept_name: Recovery Of Managerial Remuneration In Certain Cases [Section 199]
descriptors.definition: When a company must restate its financial statements due to fraud or non-compliance, it is required to recover excess remuneration paid to key personnel during the affected period. Repaying this excess does not shield the defaulting individual from additional liabilities under corporate law.
inclusion: Recovery of stock options and cash remuneration received during restated periods
Continuation of statutory liability despite remuneration payback
exclusion: Remuneration earned during accurate, unadjusted financial periods
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard remuneration forfeiture from fraud-triggered financial restatement clawbacks

descriptors.definition: Net profits for calculating maximum managerial remuneration are derived by adding specific government subsidies and excluding capital profits, share premiums, and unrealized fair value gains. Fixed asset sales contribute to profits only up to the difference between original cost and written-down value.
inclusion: Government bounties and operational subsidies added to profit
Adjustments for fixed asset sales above written-down value
exclusion: Profits from share premiums, forfeited shares, and capital transformations
Fair value changes and unrealized revaluation gains
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates operational profits eligible for managerial commission from capital and unrealized gains

descriptors.concept_name: Forms Of, And Procedure In Relation To, Certain Applications [Section 201]
descriptors.definition: When an appointment of an older managing director fails to secure a special resolution despite majority support, the company must apply to the Central Government. The process requires filing specific forms within ninety days along with proof of publishing general notices in local newspapers.
instrument_references: Rule 7 of Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014
inclusion: Submitting Form MR-2 within ninety days of appointment
Mandatory English and regional newspaper publication of notices
exclusion: Applications for managerial remuneration which no longer require prior approval
nearby_distinctions: Separates standard shareholder-approved appointments from government regularization procedures

descriptors.concept_name: Compensation For Loss Of Office Of Managing Or Whole-Time Director Or Manager [Section 202]
descriptors.definition: Companies may compensate managing directors, whole-time directors, or managers for loss of office, restricted to the remuneration they would have earned for the remainder of their term or three years, whichever is shorter. Compensation is prohibited if the departure stems from voluntary resignation, company winding-up due to negligence, or verified fraud.
inclusion: Payments made for retirement or premature termination of managerial office
Capping payout duration at three years or remaining term
exclusion: Payments when an officer resigns voluntarily or due to proven fraud and mismanagement
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes legitimate contract termination compensation from forfeiture due to default or fraud

descriptors.definition: Certain large public companies and all listed entities must conduct a secretarial audit performed by a practicing company secretary. The resulting audit report must be annexed to the board report, with directors required to provide full explanations for any qualifications or observations made.
instrument_references: Rule 9 of Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014
inclusion: Listed companies and public companies meeting capital, turnover, or loan thresholds
Mandatory annexing of Form MR-3 audit reports to the board report
exclusion: Smaller unlisted companies falling below prescribed financial and borrowing limits
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates routine internal compliance checks from formal statutory secretarial audits

descriptors.concept_name: Managerial Remuneration Under Schedule V Special Circumstances
descriptors.definition: Companies with no or inadequate profits may pay managerial remuneration exceeding standard limits under specific special circumstances. These exceptions apply to newly incorporated entities for seven years, sick or revived companies, and entities executing resolution plans under the insolvency framework.
instrument_references: Schedule V of the Companies Act, 2013
inclusion: Remuneration flexibility for new businesses during their initial seven years
Paucity limits overridden by approved revival or insolvency schemes
exclusion: Established profitable companies governed strictly by standard profit percentage caps
nearby_distinctions: Separates standard profit-based payout rules from rehabilitation-period remuneration exceptions
